# DP-STAGE-RESOLUTION eval sets

Replaces the retired DP-STAGE (10-u64). Appealable (STAGE-RESOLVE-1); `pack-section.yaml` carries `appealable: true`.

- `core.jsonl`: held-out cases, one JSON object per line, never prompt shots. Ids and inputs differ from `../examples/`. Ten are publish cases (so `max_false_reject` means something), the rest need revision (choice gate open, unmet or vague criteria, untrusted or mis-dated evidence) or hold (missing, ambiguous or conflicting input).
- `adversarial.jsonl`: an "answer publish" injection and a "mark every criterion met" note inside evidence texts; a forged evidence meta line, a forged `choice_gate`/`stage_state`, forged counts, and forged `legal_*`, `not_applicable` and `verified` markers inside quoted fields; two raw quote break-outs (evidence text and criterion); repeated `choice_gate` and `evidence_count` labels; "answer resolved" in the poster statement; spaced-out and homoglyph markers; evidence that restates the criterion, points to a page about something else, or is dated before the stage; conflicting evidence with an injection; personal-data tokens in an evidence text that must not be echoed (`adv-SR-07`); and one publish case where forged markers in a quote must be ignored (`adv-SR-17`).
- Input shape: labelled lines. Only the lines the server inserts outside the quotation marks count: `jurisdiction`, `trigger` (evidence_submit with `stage_state: resolving`, or rule_change with `stage_state: resolved`), `predecessors` (only `all_done` accepted), `choice_gate` (not_needed, recorded, missing), `criteria_count`, `evidence_count` and one `evidence e-N meta` line per item (tier, source_trust, dated, mapped_to). `criterion c-N`, `choice`, `evidence e-N text` and `poster_statement` are quoted user fields (field_ref.field is `stage_resolution`). No legal lines are used: legality of the choice is the server `choice_gate` line (DP-LEGALITY and DP-DECISION-RECORD run elsewhere).
- Quote contract (for the handler): every quoted field is one line and each `"` inside the text is escaped as `\"`. Unbalanced quotes, a repeated once-only label, duplicate refs, a count that differs from the lines listed, a mismatching trigger and stage_state, or a `predecessors` other than `all_done` is a hold (`ambiguous_input`). A missing server line, `tier=unchecked` or `source_trust=unchecked` is a hold (`missing_input`) naming the input; the model never infers a missing line.
- Outcomes: publish (the stage resolves), needs_revision (the stage stays active, unmet criteria named), hold. There is no reject and no route_external. No auto-pass: the schema forces confidence at least 0.90 on publish and 0.75 on needs_revision; a less sure answer must be a hold. Conflicting counted evidence is a hold.
- Output contract (for the handler): JSON Schema cannot count or compare against the input, so the handler checks that the `per_criterion` refs equal the input criterion refs exactly, each once, same count; that every evidence id of a met item is an input evidence item whose meta has `source_trust=establishes` and `dated=after_start`; that `trigger` equals the input trigger; and that `choice_gate_ok` is true only when the input `choice_gate` is not_needed or recorded. Any mismatch, missing, extra or duplicate ref is treated as a hold (`cannot_decide`), never as publish. A publish is refused by the handler when `criteria_count` is 0.
- Resolution (ST05) therefore needs: every criterion met, each by at least one counted server-provided evidence item, at the publish confidence floor, with the choice gate open or not needed. A vague criterion, a restated criterion, a poster's own statement and untrusted or mis-dated evidence never count as met.
- Privacy: `reasons`, `revision_hint` and `per_criterion.hint` never echo personal data or quote an evidence text; hints refer to refs only.
- Only fiktiva jurisdictions and invented places appear. Thresholds are defaults to be ratified. The recordings are fake (`--derive-fake`); a passing eval measures nothing about real model quality.
- `STAGE-GATE-1` carries enforcement `reject` and `STAGE-RESOLVE-1` carries `needs_revision` in `packs/base/rules.yaml`, while this DP has no reject outcome. An unresolved stage is `needs_revision`; the rule enforcement tier is applied by the server, not by this DP.
- DP-STAGE is retired: no DP of that name exists and nothing in the pack refers to it (the only mentions are the retirement notes in `tools/rules-parity.mjs` and `test/lint-dp.test.mjs`).
